abilities.label: Buggerhead's Redraw
abilities.sourceText: While in play, Buggerhead allows you to discard and redraw any 1 sept card at the end of your normal Redraw Phase.

abilities.label: Veterinarian's Care
abilities.sourceText: During you Regeneration Phase, the Veterinarian can cure 1 additional damage card (including an aggravated wound) from 1 character in your pack.

abilities.label: Grand Klaive (Crinos bonus)
abilities.sourceText: When in Crinos form, the owner acts at +1 Rage.
abilities.note: Grand Klaive's other clause (all damage it deals is aggravated) is a combat-engine concern, not scripted here yet.

abilities.label: Dodge (avoid the incoming attack)
abilities.sourceText: Avoids one attack. Choose one damage card played this round on the character who has dodged and discard it.
abilities.note: Full text lets the dodger choose WHICH incoming card to avoid when several creatures are attacking (pack combat). V1's single-attacker-vs-single-defender scope means there's never more than one candidate, so 'choose' collapses to 'the one card played against this character this round, if any'. Revisit if/when pack combat is built.

abilities.label: Evasion (avoid all attacks this round)
abilities.sourceText: Avoids (dodges) all attacks during the current combat round.
abilities.note: Same V1 simplification as Dodge — 'all attacks' collapses to 'the one incoming card, if any' until pack combat exists. Functionally identical to Dodge at this scope; kept as its own scripted entry for textual fidelity and because it costs more Rage (2 vs 1).

abilities.label: Evade and Strike (dodge + attack)
abilities.sourceText: Kailindo. You can dodge all attacks this round, except those that normally ignore dodges.
abilities.note: Also a normal Rage 3 / Damage 1 Combat Action in its own right — that half needs no scripting, applyDamage() already deals its printed damage like any other card. This entry is purely the defensive half. 'Except those that normally ignore dodges' = Undodgeable, already handled generically in combat.js via hasKeyword(card, 'Undodgeable').

abilities.label: Head Wound (no Combat Action next round)
abilities.sourceText: A victim damaged by this attack may not play any Combat Actions during the next round of combat.
abilities.note: Errata clarifies the wounded creature may still withdraw between rounds if it's the attacker — nothing extra to script for that, since withdrawal was already not a 'Combat Action' by the base rules (rule 3.3's Actions/actions distinction), so combat.js's WITHDRAW offering was never gated by this flag in the first place.

abilities.label: Organ Puncture (cannot initiate combat until healed)
abilities.sourceText: A character damaged by the Organ Puncture cannot initiate combat until this wound is healed. He can, however, defend if attacked.

abilities.label: Overextended Attack (self: no Combat Action next round)
abilities.sourceText: Your character may not play a Combat Action next round.

abilities.label: Overextended Attack (self: cannot withdraw this round)
abilities.sourceText: If your character is the attacker, she may not withdraw before the next round.
abilities.note: combat.js only ever offers WITHDRAW to the attacker, so checking this flag generically already satisfies the card's own 'if your character is the attacker' condition — a defender carrying it is never offered WITHDRAW anyway, flag or not.

abilities.label: Eyes Gouged (forced random play next round)
abilities.sourceText: A victim damaged by this attack is temporarily blinded. The victim must attack with a random draw from his combat hand during the next combat round.

abilities.label: Run Like Hell (flee, ending combat)
abilities.sourceText: When this card is played on a character, she immediately flees, exiting combat.
abilities.note: V1's single-attacker-vs-single-defender scope means one side fleeing always ends the whole combat (rule 6.3: combat ends when either side has no combatants) — same observable effect as Forceful Wind, hence the shared marker. Checked directly in combat.js AFTER the round's tiered resolution completes (so the opponent's card has already resolved first, matching 'this effect takes place after your opponent's Combat Action is resolved'), not via onDamageDealt — Run Like Hell has no Damage value, so applyDamage() would never fire for it. The Moot/Junta voting restriction ('cannot vote until she has fought that foe again') is NOT modeled — voting doesn't exist in the engine yet. Errata replaces 'Moot' with 'Junta' terminology only, no mechanical change.

abilities.label: Forceful Wind (ends combat after this round)
abilities.sourceText: Kailindo. Combat immediately ends after both sides have dealt damage.
abilities.note: Errata clarifies this fires after ALL of this round's played cards have resolved, not literally 'both sides' (relevant now that more than one card per side is possible via Feint). Shares the endsCombatAfterRound marker with Run Like Hell — checked directly in combat.js after the tiered resolution loop, independent of whether Forceful Wind's own damage actually landed (e.g. even if dodged or pre-empted by a faster kill).

abilities.label: Surprise Attack (round 1: cancels the opponent's damage back)
abilities.sourceText: If this card damages an opponent during the first round of combat, the victim will inflict no damage this round.
abilities.note: Errata: mutual Surprise Attacks cancel each other — each side's own connection is checked independently against the round's original resolution, so the two cancellations don't chain or depend on processing order. Also per errata, cannot cancel a Fast Striking opponent's damage unless Surprise Attack was itself Fast Striking — enforced with the same SPEED_RANK comparison used for Dodge legality. The final errata clause ('Surprise Attack only prevents damage') is partly garbled in the source data; implemented here as a full retroactive undo of the opponent's wound and anything conditionally scripted off it, on the reading that a fully prevented wound should leave no partial trace — flagged as a judgment call in case a narrower reading was intended.

abilities.label: Telling Blow (+3 VP if it's the killing blow)
abilities.sourceText: If the damage from this card immediately kills your opponent, place Telling Blow in your victory pile for an additional 3 victory points.
abilities.note: Errata: must be THE killing blow specifically — tracked during combat.js's tiered resolution loop as the first card, in resolution order, whose damage pushes a creature from alive to dead, not just any card played by the killer that round. Redirected to the Victory Pile in place of the normal combat discard, worth a flat +3 VP via an instance-level vpOverride (Combat Actions have no printed Renown for countVP() to read otherwise). The Prey-creature exception ('If a Prey Creature kills someone with a Telling Blow, TB has no special effect') isn't modeled — Prey aren't yet playable combat participants in this engine.

abilities.label: Feint (follow-up after seeing the opponent's card)
abilities.sourceText: You may play any Combat Action in immediate response to your opponent's Combat Action.
abilities.note: Errata: 'Feint may not be bluffed' — the follow-up chance requires Feint to have been legally played (Rage 4+), not just revealed; see canFeint() in combat.js, which checks isLegalCombatCard() directly rather than waiting for the later Bluff step. 'This card played after seeing opponent's card targets the same creature as the Feint' is automatic in V1's single-attacker-vs-single-defender scope — there's only one possible target either way. Only one follow-up card is allowed even if a multiple-Combat-Action effect is also in play, per Feint's own errata.

abilities.label: Fur Gnarl (Crinos wound)
abilities.sourceText: If the victim takes this wound in Crinos form, this damage is aggravated.
abilities.note: Errata: the check happens once, at the moment the wound lands — aggravated status doesn't change if the victim later shifts to breed form. That's why the engine evaluates onDamageDealt abilities BEFORE the post-damage Crinos-flip check (see combat.js/cardEngine.js), so a hit that itself triggers the flip is correctly read as landing pre-flip.

abilities.label: Broken Limb (Rage debuff)
abilities.sourceText: If damaged by this attack, the victim plays all of her Combat Actions at -2 Rage for the duration of the combat.

abilities.label: Disembowelment (Rage debuff)
abilities.sourceText: Your victim plays Combat Actions at -1 Rage until this wound is healed.

abilities.label: Off-balanced Attack (self debuff)
abilities.sourceText: The character playing this card plays Combat Actions at -1 Rage for the next round of combat.
abilities.note: Text applies to 'the character playing this card', not conditioned on the attack connecting — hooked via onDamageDealt anyway since V1 has no dodge/block yet, so a legally-played damaging card always reaches applyDamage(). Revisit once Dodge/Block exists: a dodged Off-balanced Attack should still self-debuff, and this won't fire for a dodged one.

abilities.label: Stinging Wound (Rage buff)
abilities.sourceText: If your opponent is damaged by this attack, he may play Combat Actions at +1 Rage for the next round.

abilities.label: Nerve Cluster (Rage set to 1)
abilities.sourceText: For the rest of the combat, the victim of a Nerve Cluster is considered to have a Rage of 1 when playing Combat Actions.

abilities.label: Vital Blow (Rage set to 1)
abilities.sourceText: For the next round of combat, your opponent is considered to have a Rage of 1 for the purposes of playing Combat Actions.

abilities.label: Battle Song
abilities.sourceText: The Galliard's pack plays Combat Actions at +2 Rage for the current turn. Discard this Gift after its effect takes place.
abilities.note: Simplified reading: the whole pack benefits if it contains a Galliard, rather than resolving exactly who 'the Galliard's pack' refers to.

abilities.label: Mokole Hide
abilities.sourceText: The owner of this fetish gains +2 Health. A character cannot have more than 1 Mokole Hide at a time.
abilities.note: Unconditional — omitting 'condition' means it always applies while equipped. The 'only 1 at a time' restriction isn't enforced (no resource-phase card checks play restrictions yet, matching the existing simplification level).

abilities.label: Portable Computer
abilities.sourceText: A portable computer gives its user +2 Gnosis.
abilities.note: Only the passive +2 Gnosis is scripted. 'Discard at any time to look at an opponent's hand' is an activated ability — a trigger kind that doesn't exist yet. Also unenforced: 'Can only be used by a Glass Walker'.

abilities.label: Tim Rowantree (caern Rage bonus)
abilities.sourceText: If Tim's pack gets a caern, Tim gains +2 Rage and +1 Health.

abilities.label: Tim Rowantree (caern Health bonus)
abilities.sourceText: If Tim's pack gets a caern, Tim gains +2 Rage and +1 Health.

abilities.label: Blood-on-the-Wind (Wendigo pack bonus)
abilities.sourceText: All Wendigo in the same pack as Blood-on-the-Wind gain +1 Rage.

abilities.label: Gunnar Draugrbane (Rage)
abilities.sourceText: Can change into Crinos form whenever and as often as you choose. +4 Rage, +5 Health. Weakness: Gunnar cannot use any Gifts.
abilities.note: Only the flat +4 Rage / +5 Health are scripted. Unenforced: unrestricted Crinos flipping, and the 'no new Gifts' weakness (no restriction/prohibition verb exists yet).

abilities.label: Gunnar Draugrbane (Health)
abilities.sourceText: Can change into Crinos form whenever and as often as you choose. +4 Rage, +5 Health. Weakness: Gunnar cannot use any Gifts.

abilities.label: Old Red Eagle (Gnosis)
abilities.sourceText: Each pack member can regenerate an extra damage card during the Regeneration Phase. +4 Gnosis. Weakness: -3 Health (never less than 1).

abilities.label: Old Red Eagle (Health penalty)
abilities.sourceText: Each pack member can regenerate an extra damage card during the Regeneration Phase. +4 Gnosis. Weakness: -3 Health (never less than 1).
abilities.note: effectiveHealth() already floors at 1 (Math.max(1, ...)), so 'never less than 1' falls out for free.

abilities.label: Old Red Eagle's Blessing
abilities.sourceText: Each pack member can regenerate an extra damage card during the Regeneration Phase. +4 Gnosis. Weakness: -3 Health (never less than 1).
abilities.note: Reuses the same verb as Kinfolk Veterinarian's ability. Text says 'each pack member CAN' (i.e. one extra heal per pack member, not just one total) — simplified here to grant one extra-heal choice per source card in play, same as the Vet. Worth a second look.

abilities.label: Unicorn's Blessing
abilities.sourceText: One pack member may regenerate 1 additional damage card during your Regeneration Phase. A pack may not have more than 1 Pack Totem at any time.
abilities.note: Same verb as Kinfolk Veterinarian's ability. Required an Event play-pathway fix (Events had no legal-action branch at all until this batch). 'No more than 1 Pack Totem' unenforced, matching the existing simplification level for play restrictions.

abilities.label: War Paint of Wahya Ohni
abilities.sourceText: When applied, the Garou heals twice as quickly. Remove 1 additional damage card from the owner of this fetish during the Regeneration Phase.
abilities.note: New targetScope:'holder' option — unlike the Vet/Unicorn/Old Red Eagle (choose any pack member), this always heals whoever's wearing it, never a free choice.

abilities.label: Mother's Touch
abilities.sourceText: This Gift heals the lowest damage card from the target, up to a damage 4 card. This Gift will heal aggravated damage. Discard this Gift after its effect takes place.
abilities.note: First card using a play-time target rather than 'whole pack' or 'holder'. Reuses the existing Gift target pool (own pack/allies only) — no targetRequirement needed since it doesn't cross the player boundary. The 'up to damage 4' cap isn't enforced; regenerate() already heals the lowest card first, so this only matters in edge cases.

abilities.label: Inbred Disorder
abilities.sourceText: Choose 1 Silver Fangs. The character suffers from a slight mental abnormality. She acts at -2 Gnosis for the rest of the game. A character may not be affected by more than 1 Inbred Disorder.
abilities.note: First card targeting across the player boundary — Silver Fangs on either side are eligible, not just the caster's own pack. Reuses the existing static/attachment machinery unchanged once attached. 'May not be affected by more than 1' isn't enforced, matching the existing simplification level for play restrictions.

abilities.label: Curse of Hatred
abilities.sourceText: The character looks into his opponent's eyes and focuses his hatred, disheartening his foe. The target plays her next Combat Action at -2 Rage. Discard this Gift after its effect takes place.
abilities.note: Simplified 'next Combat Action' to 'until end of turn' (same simplification as Battle Song) — rageMod is already cleared once per turn by the existing clearTurnModifiers(), and there's no per-card-play cleanup hook to expire it after exactly one combat action instead.

abilities.label: Whelp Body
abilities.sourceText: The target of this Gift acts at -3 Rage. The target's Rage may never drop below 1 as a result of this Gift. This Gift lasts until canceled.
abilities.note: The floor-of-1 (rather than the engine's default floor-of-0) isn't enforced. 'Until canceled' has no cancel mechanism yet, so this is effectively permanent once attached — same simplification as Inbred Disorder.

abilities.label: Take the True Form
abilities.sourceText: The user forces any shapechanger to revert to his breed form. If this kills the character in combat, the victim's opponent gains victory points for the kill. Discard this Gift after its effect takes place.
abilities.note: Only the core force-flip is scripted (reuses flipToBreed()). The victory-points-for-a-kill clause and the 2014 errata (counterable by flipping to Crinos/Frenzy in response) aren't implemented — both need capabilities (death-triggered VP, response windows) that don't exist yet.

abilities.label: Serenity
abilities.sourceText: This Gift cancels a frenzy. Discard this Gift after its effect takes place.
abilities.note: Nothing currently sets frenzied=true — Song of Rage, the natural pairing, needed a caster-vs-target Gnosis comparison the targeting system doesn't support yet, so it's deferred rather than approximated. Tested here with a synthetic frenzied instance.

abilities.label: Alaskan Wolf Hunt
abilities.sourceText: Humans are exterminating native wolves. Red Talons are caught in the hunt. All Red Talons characters must go into the Hunting Grounds until the next Regeneration Phase. Only 1 Alaskan Wolf Hunt may be played per game.
abilities.note: Affects every Red Talons character on both sides, not just the caster's — this is an external event, not a directed attack. Modeled as removed-from-play generally rather than physically placed in GameState.huntingGrounds, since that array is already treated as attackable prey by getCombatActions() — reusing it would let the opponent attack someone who's supposed to be untouchable. 'Only 1 per game' unenforced, matching established precedent for play restrictions.

abilities.label: Ragnarok
abilities.sourceText: The Get of Fenris believe that the Final Battle is upon them. All Get of Fenris go to the Hunting Grounds until the next Regeneration Phase. Only 1 Ragnarok can be played per game.
abilities.note: Same shape as Alaskan Wolf Hunt, different tribe.

abilities.label: Burrow
abilities.sourceText: The user burrows into the ground to escape combat. The Metis may not be attacked or called out until she comes out, and may not take any actions during this time. The Metis comes out at the beginning of the next Regeneration Phase. Discard this Gift after its effect takes place.
abilities.note: Source data for this card was truncated at 'Discard this Gift after'; Project Lead verified the complete text directly, confirming the discardSelf inference was correct. 'May not be attacked or take actions' falls out for free from being physically removed from the pack array. Doesn't yet end an in-progress combat the character might be in — that needs combat.js integration.

abilities.label: Moon Bridge Escape
abilities.sourceText: The Gift user gives any 1 willing character or pack passage over a Moon Bridge. Characters are immediately removed from play until the next Redraw Phase. Discard this Gift after its effect takes place.
abilities.note: Only the single-character case is scripted; the 'or pack' whole-pack removal option isn't. Also doesn't yet end an in-progress combat the target might be in, per the card's own errata clarification — that needs combat.js integration, same gap as Burrow.

abilities.label: Greater Banishment
abilities.sourceText: The user cancels any Gift. Remove the target Gift from play. Discard this Gift after its effect takes place.
abilities.note: First card targeting an attached card instance rather than a character — new targetRequirement scope 'anyAttachment'. No Gnosis-cost ceiling on the target, unlike the two variants below.

abilities.label: Lesser Banishment
abilities.sourceText: The user cancels any 1 Gift that requires Gnosis 5 or less. Remove the target Gift from play. Discard this Gift after its effect takes place.

abilities.label: Remove Gaia's Blessing
abilities.sourceText: The user cancels any 1 Gift that requires Gnosis 7 or less. Remove the target Gift from play. Discard this Gift after its effect takes place.

abilities.label: Jam Technology
abilities.sourceText: The character may disable any 1 non-fetish item. The chosen item is immediately discarded. Discard this Gift after its effect takes place.
abilities.note: 'Non-fetish' restriction unenforced — Equipment has no structured fetish/non-fetish subtype in the data (even Mokole Hide, whose own text calls it 'this fetish', is just Type:'Equipment').

abilities.label: Anna-Eyes (voting Renown)
abilities.sourceText: Anna has +1 Renown for moot votes.

abilities.label: Cernonous (voting Renown penalty)
abilities.sourceText: Cernonous is considered -1 Renown for moot voting due to his Metis disfigurement.

abilities.label: Grek Twice-Tongue (voting Renown)
abilities.sourceText: Despite his Metis breed, Grek is considered +1 Renown for moot voting.

abilities.label: Grimfang (voting Renown)
abilities.sourceText: Grimfang is considered +3 Renown for moot voting.

abilities.label: Pearl River (voting Renown)
abilities.sourceText: Pearl is considered +2 Renown for moot voting.

abilities.label: Yuri Tvarivich (voting Renown)
abilities.sourceText: +8 Renown for any moot votes. +1 Health. Weakness: None.

abilities.label: Yuri Tvarivich (Health)
abilities.sourceText: +8 Renown for any moot votes. +1 Health. Weakness: None.

abilities.label: Glib Tongue
abilities.sourceText: This Gift gives the user +5 Renown for the current moot vote. Discard this Gift after its effect takes place.
abilities.note: Simplified from a one-shot 'current vote only' boost to a permanent static bonus. A true one-shot needs the Gift to stay attached until a moot is actually called (which happens later, in a different phase, as a separate action) and only then discard — that's a real timing gap, not just an unenforced restriction, so it's been simplified rather than partially implemented.

abilities.label: Persuasion
abilities.sourceText: The user of this Gift gains +1 Renown for moot voting. This Gift lasts until canceled.
abilities.note: 'Until canceled' has no cancel mechanism yet, so effectively permanent — same simplification as Inbred Disorder/Whelp Body.

abilities.label: Rite of Investiture
abilities.sourceText: Play at the end of a Moot Phase in which 1 of your characters successfully called a moot. You may select any 1 ally and make him a full member of your pack. As such, that ally may now take any action, including voting in moots, that any other pack member may take.
abilities.note: First card using checkPlayCondition and the new Rite play-pathway. Simplified 'at the end of a Moot Phase' to 'any time during the Moot Phase, once a moot has passed' — offering it only at the literal end would need a phase-exit hook that doesn't exist yet, and the practical effect (the ally is promoted before combat) is the same either way.

abilities.label: Carla Grimsson (forced Crinos)
abilities.sourceText: If a moot called by Carla's pack does not pass, she shifts to Crinos and must be alpha for that turn's Combat Phase.
abilities.note: First card using the new onMootOutcome trigger. Pack-scoped per the card text ('a moot called by Carla's pack', not 'a moot Carla herself called') — fires for any failed moot her pack calls, matching how doCallMoot's tally is pack-level, not attributed to a specific caller.

abilities.label: Carla Grimsson (forced alpha)
abilities.sourceText: If a moot called by Carla's pack does not pass, she shifts to Crinos and must be alpha for that turn's Combat Phase.
abilities.note: New forceAlpha verb — enterCombat() now checks for a forced alpha before falling back to the normal highest-Renown auto-selection. Single-turn: the flag clears itself once consumed.

abilities.label: Falcon (pack-wide voting Renown)
abilities.sourceText: Each pack member gains 1 Renown for moot voting. A pack may not have more than 1 Pack Totem at any time.
abilities.note: First pack-wide bonus sourced from an Event rather than a character or attachment — packWideBonus's source pool now includes played events. No keyword filter (applies to the whole pack unconditionally). 'No more than 1 Pack Totem' unenforced, matching precedent.

abilities.label: Fenris (pack-wide Rage in Crinos)
abilities.sourceText: All pack members gain 1 Rage when in Crinos form. A pack may not have more than 1 Pack Totem at any time.
abilities.note: Combines the unconditional pack-wide scope with the existing holderIsCrinos condition (previously only used for a single equipped character, e.g. Grand Klaive) — same condition check, now applied per pack member.

abilities.label: Pegasus (pack-wide Gnosis)
abilities.sourceText: Each pack member gains 1 Gnosis. A pack may not have more than 1 Pack Totem at any time.

abilities.label: Rat (pack-wide Health)
abilities.sourceText: Each pack member gains 1 Health. A pack may not have more than 1 Pack Totem at any time.

abilities.label: Chimera
abilities.sourceText: Increases your sept hand size by 1. A pack may not have more than 1 Pack Totem at any time.
abilities.note: First effect touching player-level state rather than a character stat — new increasePlayerStat verb, a direct one-time mutation rather than a continuously-queried modifier, since septHandSize isn't recomputed per-character the way Rage/Gnosis are.

abilities.label: Elder Stone
abilities.sourceText: The owner of this stone gains an additional 3 votes during any moot. The owner can discard this stone during a moot and gain an additional 10 votes. A character cannot have more than 1 Elder Stone at a time.
abilities.note: 'Votes' mapped onto VotingRenown, the same currency doCallMoot already tallies — a reasonable rename rather than building a separate 'votes' concept for one card. Only the passive +3 is scripted; the discard-for-+10 option is an activated ability, a trigger kind that doesn't exist yet (same gap as Portable Computer's peek ability).

abilities.label: Kinfolk TV Reporter
abilities.sourceText: Your pack gains 2 votes during all moots while the TV Reporter is in play, due to his ability to sway public opinion around events.
abilities.note: Pack-wide bonus sourced from an Ally rather than an Event or character — same extended packWideBonus source pool as the Totem cards.

abilities.label: Hunting Party (pack attack)
abilities.sourceText: Play when your character is declaring an attack. For attacks against nonalpha characters, Hunting Party must be played before the challenge is accepted or declined. Select members of your pack to join the attack. You can have a total of 15 Renown of characters in the attack (including the original character). Draw 1 additional combat card per additional pack member.
abilities.note: Rule 6.5.8 explicitly names this (along with Attacking the Wyrm and Ass Whuppin' Lynch Mob, neither scripted yet) as playable ONLY during the Declaration step — the general pack-action window (precombat/beginCombat/betweenRounds) does not apply to it. Renown cap of 15 includes the original alpha already in the attack, so the engine only needs to fill the REMAINING headroom (15 - the alpha's own Renown). Two things flagged for later rather than handled now, since neither mechanic exists in the engine yet: (1) the card's own text ties its declaration-step window to challenges specifically — 'before the challenge is accepted or declined' — but challenges (rule 6.5.2, attacking a non-alpha who may decline) aren't implemented at all yet, so there's no decline step to race against; the current single Declaration pause already fires before where a decline step would go, once one exists. (2) Errata: 'creatures may step in after the attack has been declared so would have to face your pack' — stepping in (rule 6.5.9) isn't implemented either; when it is, it needs to check the FINAL post-Hunting-Party participants list, not just the original alpha.

abilities.label: Pack Defense (pack defense)
abilities.sourceText: Play before one of your defending characters begins combat. You may pull members from your pack into the combat, up to 15 Renown worth of characters (including the original character). You may draw 1 additional combat card per additional pack member.
abilities.note: Errata clarifies this is played specifically in the Pre-Combat step (not the wider precombat/beginCombat/betweenRounds window rule 6.5.8 grants most pack-action cards) — mechanically identical to Hunting Party otherwise (same 15-Renown cap including the original defender, same 1-card-per-extra-member draw), just for the defending side instead of the attacker.

abilities.label: Surprise Ally (pack attack, 1 member)
abilities.sourceText: Play before the first round of a combat (including right after a challenge has been accepted) or between rounds of a combat. You may draw in one additional pack member for a pack attack. Draw 1 additional combat card. Surprise Ally can only be used during combats in which your character is the attacker.
abilities.note: Attacker-only, unlike Bum Rush which either side can play. Brings in exactly one additional member (not a Renown-capped selection like Hunting Party/Pack Defense) and is permanent for the rest of the combat — no auto-escape, unlike Bum Rush.

abilities.label: Bum Rush (whole pack, one round only)
abilities.sourceText: Play at the beginning of any combat round before combat action cards are exchanged. Each member of the character's pack comes forward to join the combat for the upcoming round only. At the end of the combat round, the pack withdraws from combat, leaving only the original character.
abilities.note: Errata: 'Creatures that came forward for a Bum Rush ESCAPE at the end of round rather than withdraw' — modeled as duration:'round', resolved in resolveExpiredPackActions('round') at the top of startNextRound(), distinct from death (no VP, no killing-blow bookkeeping, no Victory Pile). No bonus cards drawn, unlike the other three join cards — the whole pack has to share the player's existing combat hand for that one round, which is the real cost of bringing everyone in at once. Playable by either side, unlike Surprise Ally/Hunting Party (attacker-only) or Pack Defense (defender-only).

abilities.label: Shieldmate (pack defense, 1 member, redirect choice)
abilities.sourceText: Play this card when 1 of your characters is attacked. 1 packmate joins your character in pack defense as a shieldmate. Draw 1 additional combat card. You may choose whether your opponent's Combat Actions are played on the defender or the shieldmate.
abilities.note: Reuses the same packJoin engine as Hunting Party/Pack Defense/Surprise Ally for the join itself (1 fixed member, declaration step, defender-only — same shape as Surprise Ally but for the defending side reacting to being attacked, matching rule 6.1's Declaration step framing: 'Defending player...uses abilities or cards played during the attack declaration (Shieldmate is the only card at present)'). The createsShieldmateGroup flag is the part that's genuinely different: per errata ('Whenever the attacker assigns a Combat Action or face-down combat card to the defender or shieldmate, you can choose either as the target'), this INVERTS rule 6.7's normal default — instead of the attacker choosing which of the two defenders their card hits, the defender's own controller does, fresh each round. Implemented in combat.js's targeting step (findShieldmateGroup), not as a separate mechanic of its own.

abilities.label: Taking the Death Blow (redirect a mortal wound)
abilities.sourceText: Play this card when 1 of your characters receives a mortal wound. Select another member of your pack to take the wound instead. Combat may continue with the new pack member in place of the old. The new pack member is considered to be alpha for the remainder of the Combat Phase.
abilities.note: Errata (rageccg.weebly.com/spoilers.html, confirmed with the project owner — the copy of this errata in rage_cards.json was truncated mid-sentence): 'Taking the Death Blow can only be used if both creatures could be in a pack action. This effect will not cross the Gauntlet. The original target of the attack escapes combat if able. If not, it creates a pack action. The creature using Taking the Death Blow always becomes Alpha if used during the combat phase. TtDB can only redirect damage cards: it cannot be played in response to effects which lower health or force a shapeshift. See rules on Redirecting Attacks.' Implemented as a reactive pause between damage resolution and checkCombatDeaths() — see checkForDeathBlowOpportunities()/playDeathBlowRedirect() in combat.js. Redirects the SPECIFIC fatal card only (Phase 3's killingBlowFor already identifies exactly which one — the same attribution Telling Blow's bonus uses), not the creature's other wounds. 'Escapes if able' always succeeds today since no card yet grants a 'cannot escape' flag; the 'stays and creates a pack action instead' branch exists in code but is unreachable until one does. The damage-cards-only restriction is automatically satisfied today — isDead() only ever checks accumulated damage cards, and no direct-health-reduction or forced-shapeshift-death mechanic exists in the engine yet; revisit this note if either is ever scripted. Pack-action eligibility (Rivalry-style exclusions) and Gauntlet-matching aren't separately checked — neither Rivalry nor multi-side-of-Gauntlet combat is modeled anywhere else in the engine yet either, so this isn't a gap specific to this card.

abilities.label: Mindspeak (grants standing pack-join permission between 2 creatures)
abilities.sourceText: The user communicates telepathically with 1 other member of her pack. The user and her packmate may join in pack attacks or defenses for the remainder of the turn. Draw 1 additional combat card if these characters enter combat. Discard this Gift after its effect takes place.
abilities.note: Structurally different from the other five Phase 4 cards: a Gift (playable any time, rule 4.5.3 — NOT step-restricted like a Combat Event), and it doesn't join anyone to combat immediately. It grants two specific creatures standing PERMISSION to join together later, 'for the remainder of the turn' — matching rule 6.5.8's framing of a card-granted ability to 'join in pack attack or defence,' usable 'even if that creature was brought into pack combat by some other means,' at the GENERAL default timing (precombat/beginCombat/betweenRounds), since the card's own text doesn't restrict further. Implementation is split across two files: turnManager.js's doPlayGiftPackLink() handles the out-of-combat play (generates one action per valid (user, packmate) pair, filtered by the card's own Requires keyword — Galliard — and Gnosis requirement, via the SAME effectiveGnosis() helper other Gift plays already use; the Gift itself discards immediately, since the linking IS its effect) and records {a, b, bonusCards, grantedBy} on ps.packLinks; combat.js's eligiblePackLinks()/JOIN_LINKED_PACKMATE then checks, whenever a combat exists, whether one linked creature is already a participant and offers to bring in the other, drawing the bonus card only at that point ('if these characters enter combat') and consuming the link. ps.packLinks clears at the start of every Redraw phase (turnManager.js's enterRedraw()) for the 'remainder of the turn' expiry. Two things NOT modeled, matching gaps already flagged for other cards: Rivalry-based exclusions (not implemented anywhere yet) and the general Open-Play 'announce an Offensive Effect' timing etiquette (rule 3.2.1) that would technically govern exactly when mid-turn a Gift like this gets played outside of combat.
